ceo_questions: Is the current discovery/invention engine the most efficient architecture?
Does the simplest architecture produce the best result?

repo_sediment.note: The ACTIVE engine is ~2% of the analyzed codebase; the rest is historical sediment. The sediment does not slow the engine (imports resolve to the active path) but it slows every audit, hides secrets (all 7 files with live credential material are in sediment: R354, R358, CANONICAL_STATE, worklogs), and multiplies every clone/search/review.

runtime_cost_structure.deterministic_stages: sub-second each (measured: envelope writes cluster within seconds)
runtime_cost_structure.conclusion: Efficiency for this engine == LLM call economy + transport resilience. Stage count is computationally free. Cutting stages would not measurably speed the loop; fixing transport would.

quality_outcome_structure.held_failure_pattern: each held dossier fails EXACTLY ONE dimension: SEMANTIC_CAUSAL x2 (R-02), EQUATION_APPLICABILITY x1 (R-05)
quality_outcome_structure.real_mode_sealed_set: 1/4 full loop (honest REJECTED at adversarial gate); 0 dossiers
quality_outcome_structure.conclusion: The architecture PRODUCES complete packages; the binding constraint is localized CONTENT CORRECTNESS (R-02/R-05), not missing architectural capability. More stages would not fix R-02/R-05; better generation and targeted repair will.

verdict_q1_most_efficient: NO — close, but three measured inefficiencies: (1) TRANSPORT FRAGILITY: single credentialed provider with 240s x3 serial same-provider retries; the REAL loop stalls exactly here (2/4 sealed problems transport-blocked; 1/4 synthesis took ~8 min). The 8-provider registry exists; the failover-on-timeout path does not. (2) NO TARGETED REPAIR LOOP: the quality gate runs TERMINALLY. A run failing ONE dimension pays the FULL pipeline cost and yields zero dossier (12/15 PIPELINE_FAILED; 3/15 HELD each failing exactly one dimension). Regenerating only the failing dimension would convert HELD->RELEASED at a fraction of cost. (3) SEDIMENT DRAG: 97.8% of analyzed code is historical; it is where secrets hide and where audits slow down. The core 13-stage loop itself is computationally efficient (sub-second per stage) and epistemically sound (honest kills, fail-closed) — keep it.
verdict_q2_simplest_best: EMPIRICALLY YES SO FAR, WITH ONE CAVEAT. The best results to date — the frozen 15-package portfolio and the 3 released BENCH dossiers — were produced by the SIMPLE path: curated evidence + frozen v4 builders. The full autonomous 13-stage loop has produced ZERO released dossiers at the current head (it holds 3 and honestly kills its own candidates — which is correct epistemics, not failure). The caveat: the autonomous loop's value is HONESTY (it refuses to self-certify), and its missing capability is generation-time engineering reasoning (R-02/R-05), not simplicity. The simplest architecture that produces the best result = KEEP the 13-stage loop as the honesty spine, KEEP the frozen v4 builders as the packaging layer, FIX synthesis correctness, ADD targeted single-dimension repair, ARCHIVE the sediment. Do NOT add stages; do NOT remove the adversarial gates.
